source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide where male and female gametes are found and how fertilisation happens in flowering plants and animals.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: flowering plants is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: For fish or frogs, sperm and eggs may be released into water for fertilisation.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: fertilisation setting -> zygote formation happens first, and that produces gamete location and release.

intelligence.enrichment: In flowering plants, pollen grains inside the anther are male gametes and ovules inside the flower are female gametes; in animals, sperm are male gametes and eggs are female gametes, and fertilisation may occur in water or inside the female. gamete location and release -> fertilisation setting -> zygote formation The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: In flowering plants, pollen grains inside the anther are male gametes and ovules inside the flower are female gametes; in animals, sperm are male gametes and eggs are female gametes, and fertilisation may occur in water or inside the female. Pollen is just a powder on flowers and eggs are only bird eggs, so they are not gametes.
